questionText: What is spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto and what are its values?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can explain each common ddl-auto action, identify data-loss risks, and choose versioned migrations plus validate or none for persistent production data.

claims.statement: The common ddl-auto values none, validate, update, create, and create-drop select no action, schema validation, best-effort update, startup recreation, or startup recreation plus shutdown drop respectively.
Spring Boot defaults ddl-auto to create-drop only for an embedded database when no schema manager is detected and otherwise defaults it to none.
Persistent production schemas should normally use reviewed, versioned Flyway or Liquibase migrations, with Hibernate validate or none rather than automatic create, create-drop, or update ownership.
Hibernate ORM 6.5.2.Final managed by Spring Boot 3.3.1 also recognizes lower-level hbm2ddl action names including create-only and drop beyond the five common interview values.

examples.title: Resolve the learner's action names with the Spring Boot managed Hibernate version

validation.command: Use Java 17 with Spring Boot 3.3.1 dependency management and assert Hibernate Action.interpretHbm2ddlSetting for none, validate, update, create, create-drop, create-only, and drop
validation.expected: Every documented name resolves to its corresponding Hibernate 6.5.2.Final Action

visuals.title: Five common ddl-auto actions compared by effect and suitable use

notes: The lesson calls update best effort and never promises a safe rename, column drop, migration history, or rollback.
The profile example is configuration, not a claim that enabling Flyway alone creates a complete migration plan.

review.notes: Boot defaults and migration integration were checked against Spring Boot 3.3.1; action meanings and accepted names were checked against the official Hibernate guide and executed with managed Hibernate 6.5.2.Final.
